prisoner.name: Glen Collins
prisoner.description: Glen Collins participated in the December 2012 Keystone XL pipeline protest near Winona, Texas. The protest led to several weeks in Smith County Jail before release.
affiliation: Radical Action for Mountains’ and People’s Survival (RAMPS)

cases.charges: Criminal trespass, resisting arrest and illegal dumping reported after Keystone XL blockade
cases.sentence: Arrested December 3, 2012 and held in Smith County Jail on a reported $65, 000 bond. The February 2013 interview reports twenty-four days served by the three defendants; the campaign also confirms release. The exact release day is unverified. This records the initial pretrial detention, not a sentence of twenty-four days.

cases.charges: Criminal trespass and illegal dumping — Keystone XL blockade plea
cases.sentence: Returned to Smith County Jail April 24, 2013 after pleading guilty and receiving a sixty-day sentence. The campaign initially had not resolved how the earlier pretrial custody would be credited. A later update gives a conditional future May 7 release dependent on court-cost payment; no actual release date or full sixty days served is asserted.

case_research.custody_evidence: Contemporary December12 and December20 reports establish continued detention; later participant interview confirms twenty-four days actually served and release.
Actual entry and subsequent reports of jail calls, illness and delayed books establish multi-day post-sentence custody.

prisoner.name: Camilo Pereira
prisoner.description: Camilo Pereira participated in the June 2014 blockade of Alpha Natural Resources headquarters in Bristol, Virginia. Pereira was among eight activists who spent multiple days in jail while awaiting bond hearings.
affiliation: Radical Action for Mountains’ and People’s Survival (RAMPS)

cases.charges: Alpha headquarters protest — individual counts unverified; group reports list trespass, obstructing passage, disorderly conduct and fire-code violations
cases.sentence: Arrested June 20, 2014 and still jailed with the group at the June 23 arraignment. A July 6 campaign update confirms everyone had been released. The individual release day and final charges or disposition remain unverified; no sentence is inferred from the pretrial detention.

case_research.custody_evidence: Named blockade participant tied to the following custody report; all eight remained imprisoned through the weekend and were later released.

prisoner.name: Catherine Ann MacDougal
prisoner.description: Catherine Ann MacDougal, known as Squirrel, participated in the Coal River Mountain tree sit and a coal-barge blockade in West Virginia. MacDougal wrote about jail conditions and the environmental campaign after custody in 2012.
affiliation: Radical Action for Mountains’ and People’s Survival (RAMPS)

cases.charges: Trespassing following Coal River Mountain tree sit — no-contest plea; conspiracy dropped
cases.sentence: Entered Southern Regional Jail February 9, 2012 for seven days. The campaign recorded a jail visit and a statement during the term; the February 18 first-person update confirms that the week had been served and release had occurred. Exact release day remains unverified.

cases.charges: Coal-barge protest at Chelyan — initial detention, individual statutory count unverified
cases.sentence: Spent two days in South Central Regional Jail immediately after the May 24, 2012 action. The November sentencing report expressly credits these two days against the later twenty-day sentence. The exact release day is unverified.

cases.charges: Coal-barge protest plea — remaining custody after credit; individual count unverified
cases.sentence: Returned to South Central Regional Jail November 5, 2012 to serve eighteen remaining days of a twenty-day sentence, with two earlier days credited. MacDougal rejected a proposed probation arrangement; the final agreement imposed no probation. November 20 reporting confirms continued custody, and the November 26 update confirms release. The projected Thanksgiving release is not recorded as an independently verified exact day.
